classes.description: Caused by Sclerospora graminicola. Shows as yellowish streaks on upper leaf surface with white sporulation below.

treatment.organic: Spray Trichoderma viride (4g/L water) at 10-day intervals. Remove and destroy infected plants.
treatment.chemical: Metalaxyl 35% WS seed treatment (6g/kg seed). Spray Mancozeb 75% WP (2.5g/L) at first sign.
treatment.affordable: Cow urine diluted 1:10 + neem leaf extract as foliar spray every 7 days.

classes.description: Caused by Magnaporthe grisea. Diamond-shaped lesions with gray centers and dark borders on leaves.

treatment.organic: Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens (2.5kg/ha). Spray neem oil 3% at 15-day intervals.
treatment.chemical: Tricyclazole 75% WP (0.6g/L water) spray. Seed treatment with Carbendazim 50% WP (2g/kg).
treatment.affordable: Garlic-chilli extract spray (100g garlic + 50g chilli per 10L water).

classes.description: Caused by Claviceps fusiformis. Honey-dew secretions on ears, followed by sclerotia formation.

treatment.organic: Use clean certified seed. Rogue infected panicles before sclerotia mature.
treatment.chemical: Propiconazole 25% EC (1ml/L) spray at flowering. Seed treatment with Thiram 75% WS.
treatment.affordable: Soak seeds in 20% salt solution (200g/L), discard floating seeds before sowing.

classes.description: Caused by Fusarium udum. Plants wilt suddenly, yellowing from lower leaves, browning of stem internally.

treatment.organic: Seed treatment with Trichoderma harzianum (4g/kg). Apply FYM enriched with Trichoderma in furrows.
treatment.chemical: Carbendazim 50% WP seed treatment (2g/kg). Drenching with Carbendazim 0.1% at disease onset.
treatment.affordable: Deep summer plowing + crop rotation with non-legume for 2 seasons.

classes.description: Spread by eriophyid mite. Plants show bushy appearance, no pod formation, mosaic pattern on leaves.

treatment.organic: Spray Verticillium lecanii (5g/L) to control mite vector. Use resistant varieties (BSMR 736).
treatment.chemical: Dimethoate 30% EC (1.5ml/L) to control mite at 30, 45, 60 days after sowing.
treatment.affordable: Yellow sticky traps (10/acre). Early sowing (June) to escape peak mite season.

classes.description: Water-soaked lesions on stem and branches, rapid wilting and death in waterlogged conditions.

treatment.organic: Improve drainage. Apply Trichoderma viride (4g/kg seed) as seed treatment.
treatment.chemical: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) seed treatment. Spray Dimethomorph 50% WP (1g/L).
treatment.affordable: Raised bed planting. Avoid waterlogging. Apply ash around plant base.

classes.description: Caused by complex of fungi (Fusarium, Alternaria). Pink/red to black discoloration of grain at maturity.

treatment.organic: Harvest at physiological maturity. Use resistant varieties (CSH 16).
treatment.chemical: Thiophanate methyl 70% WP (1g/L) spray at 50% flowering. Propiconazole at grain fill.
treatment.affordable: Early harvest before rains. Sun drying immediately after harvest.

classes.description: Caused by Exserohilum turcicum. Large, elliptical, straw-coloured lesions with dark borders on leaves.

treatment.organic: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens (2.5kg/ha) in 500L water. Crop rotation.
treatment.chemical: Mancozeb 75% WP (2.5g/L) spray. Propiconazole 25% EC (1ml/L) at flag leaf stage.
treatment.affordable: Remove crop debris post-harvest. Balanced NPK fertilisation (avoid excess N).

classes.description: Caused by Sporisorium sorghi. Grain replaced by smut balls covered with a persistent membrane.

treatment.organic: Use certified smut-free seed. Hot water seed treatment at 55°C for 10 minutes.
treatment.chemical: Carboxin 37.5% + Thiram 37.5% DS (3g/kg seed) or Carbendazim 50% WP (2g/kg) seed treatment.
treatment.affordable: Soak seeds in saltwater, discard floaters. Use locally available smut-resistant variety.
